narration.speaker: god
narration.text: And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh
One man heard those words, and picked up an axe. On dry ground, far from any sea, he began to build a ship.
The whole valley came to laugh. How long can one family keep building while everyone they know mocks them?
Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
Genesis does not record what the neighbours said. It does not have to. Picture a ship going up in a dry valley, days from any water.
And this is the fashion which thou shalt make it of: The length of the ark shall be three hundred cubits, the breadth of it fifty cubits, and the height of it thirty cubits.
Three hundred cubits. About four hundred and fifty feet. Every beam cut by hand, and every beam a joke to the crowd.
Year after year the laughter grew louder. Men paced out the hull and shook their heads. Children threw clods of earth at the scaffolding, and their fathers cheered.
For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark,
Feasts and weddings below, music in every camp, and nobody looking up. And up on the hill, one strange family still hammering.
Then the laughter turned to anger. Stones struck the hull. Ropes were cut on the scaffold in the dark. And still the ark grew taller.
When once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing,
Waited. Every hammer blow was one more day of mercy, one more open door, even for the people throwing stones.

narration.speaker: god
narration.text: But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark,
One night the crowd came up the hill with torches, shouting at the hull. And the old man on the scaffold did not answer them with words.
Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.
No argument. No speech. Only obedience, one board at a time, until the last peg was driven.
At dawn it stood as it was told: a window above, a door in the side, three decks within. The valley that laughed went quiet, and nobody threw another stone.
Until the flood is over, Noah never speaks a word. Peter calls him a preacher of righteousness. His sermon was the ark.
Could you keep building while everyone you know laughs? Tell me in the comments.
The full story is in the long video. Part nine tomorrow: The flood.

title: Noah Built a Ship on Dry Ground 🔨 | Noah Builds the Ark, Bible Story (KJV) #shorts
description:
Genesis 6, Noah builds the ark, read from the King James Version. Part 8 of a journey through the whole Bible, one story at a time.

Lord, when everyone around me laughs, help me keep building what You asked of me. Type Amen if you prayed this with me 🙏

Part 7: God sees the earth corrupt. Next: Part 9, the flood.

Scripture: King James Version (public domain).
Visuals: AI-generated scenes (Pavo). Narration: AI voice. Music: original, owned.
